(PP-OCRv3) engine. No GPU, no network, no vision model.
# dsh-rapidocr
**Local, offline OCR for DeepSeek Harness.**

A text-only model cannot look at an image. When a user attaches a screenshot to a
conversation, the

agent is told the file path but never sees the pixels.
`dsh-rapidocr` closes that gap **on this mach

ine**: the host reads the image
bytes, hands them to a bundled CPU OCR engine and returns plain text

ne**: the host reads the image
bytes, hands them to a bundled CPU OCR engine and returns plain text.

- **Private** — images never leave the computer. No network call at all.
- **Cheap** — no vision-mod

el tokens, no API bill.
- **Offline** — the 13 MB of ONNX weights ship inside the plugin.
- **Fast**

— a 1280×720 screen capture is recognised in roughly half a second on
an ordinary 8-core desktop CP

a 1280×720 screen capture is recognised in roughly half a second on
an ordinary 8-core desktop CPU.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The engine lives in a **separate Node process**, so a one-second inference never
blocks the Electron

UI. It is started lazily on the first call and stays warm,
so the ~410 ms model load is paid once r
ather than per image.
## Install

**Option A — Plugin market.** Once the plugin is listed in the
dsh-plugin-index market, open
DSH → *
Plugins* → *Market* and install **Local OCR (dsh-rapidocr)**.

**Option B — from a clone of this repository.** Add the package to your DSH
profile and enable the b

Restart DSH (or let the profile watcher pick the change up). The plugin then

→ Plugins* with an editable configuration row.

## Platform support

**Windows x64 only in this release.** The bundled ONNX Runtime ships as a
prebuilt `onnxruntime.dll`

for `win32/x64`; the OpenCV.js part is WASM and is
platform-neutral, but the inference backend is n

ot. On other platforms the
plugin installs but the engine fails to load — add the matching
`onnxrunt

ime-node` binary for your platform to `vendor/node_modules/` (or
publish a per-platform build) to ru

inary for your platform to `vendor/node_modules/` (or
publish a per-platform build) to run it there.
## What it recognises
| Input | Result |
| PNG (all colour types, incl. palette / RGBA), JPEG (baseline + progressive) | up to 52 MB and 40 m

egapixels per image |
| Chinese, English, digits, common punctuation | 6623-character dictionary |
|

180°-rotated text | corrected automatically |
| Printed text | yes |
| Handwriting, photos of text

at a strong angle | no |
| Image *content* (what is in the picture, tables, charts) | no — this is O
CR, not a vision model |
## Performance
Measured on an Intel i7-10700F (8 cores / 16 threads, no GPU):
| Image | Warm latency | det / cls / rec |

Cost scales with the number of text lines — roughly 120–210 ms per line, and it
is **15–25 % faster

than the Python reference implementation** of RapidOCR on the
same machine.
## Repository layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The bundle has **zero npm dependencies, zero build scripts and zero install
approvals**: every runti

me dependency is vendored under `vendor/`, and the
plugin manager can therefore install it without a

package manager ever running
a postinstall hook.
## Documentation
| Document | Contents |
| docs/evaluation.md | Why this plugin, the measured numbers, the architecture comparison and the ca

pability boundaries |
| docs/implementation.md | What was actually built, the sidecar protocol, the

pitfalls hit on the way, and the remaining known gaps |
| docs/dsh-integration.md | Evidence for the

DSH plugin API (file and line references into the host) |
| packages/dsh-rapidocr/README.md | The p
lugin's own manual: configuration, testing, layout |
## Credits

The OCR pipeline in `src/` is a port of
RapidOCR (PP-OCRv3: DBNet detection,
direction classificatio

n, CRNN recognition with CTC decoding), and the ONNX
weights are the Apache-2.0 PP-OCRv3 models. See
NOTICE for the full third-party attribution.
